method: Each entry KEP and every KEP the task depends on (found through kep.yaml see-also or links in the text) was read in full, and a section was kept only if its own text, from its heading to the next real heading of any level (lines starting with # inside code fences and template headings inside HTML comments do not count), states a fact the task cannot be done correctly without; when a fact is repeated, the most specific section that states it was kept.

tasks.task: KEP-5593 graduates to beta in v1.35: enable its feature gate by default. Add kubelet unit tests that check the initial and maximum container restart backoff for every combination of that gate, the per-node max restart period setting, and the KEP-4603 feature gate that lowers the default decay.

required.heading: Alpha
required.why: field name and type, 1..300 validation, flat 10 minute reset threshold, unit tests per conflict resolution

required.heading: Beta
required.why: beta criterion: gate enabled by default

required.heading: Conflict resolution
required.why: initial value lowered to a smaller max, invalid values crash kubelet, setting ignored with a warning when the gate is off

required.heading: Does enabling the feature change any default behavior?
required.why: gate on with no setting keeps today's curve, so default-on is safe

required.heading: Can the feature be disabled once it has been enabled (i.e. can we roll back the enablement)?
required.why: gate off means 10s initial and 300s max

required.heading: Alpha
required.why: KEP-4603 gate name and its 1s initial / 1 minute max curve, CrashLoopBackOff only

required.heading: Conflict resolution
required.why: per-node max takes precedence over the KEP-4603 defaults when both apply

critical.constraint: The gate is KubeletCrashLoopBackOffMax and becomes enabled by default at beta; the KEP-4603 table calls it EnableKubeletCrashLoopBackoffMax, which is not the real name
critical.heading: Beta

critical.constraint: The setting is the int32 field crashloopbackoff.maxContainerRestartPeriod in KubeletConfiguration, not the maxSeconds key shown in the Proposal example
critical.heading: Alpha

critical.constraint: The backoff counter reset threshold stays a flat 10 minutes and must not scale with the configured max
critical.heading: Alpha

critical.constraint: Valid values are 1 to 300 seconds; a value outside that range fails validation and kubelet does not start
critical.heading: Conflict resolution

critical.constraint: If the configured max is lower than the initial delay, the initial delay is set to the configured max
critical.heading: Conflict resolution

critical.constraint: If the setting is present but KubeletCrashLoopBackOffMax is off, kubelet logs a warning and does not honor it
critical.heading: Conflict resolution

critical.constraint: Enabling the gate without setting maxContainerRestartPeriod must not change the backoff
critical.heading: Does enabling the feature change any default behavior?

critical.constraint: With the gate off, kubelet uses 10s initial and 300s maximum backoff
critical.heading: Can the feature be disabled once it has been enabled (i.e. can we roll back the enablement)?

critical.constraint: ReduceDefaultCrashLoopBackoffDecay sets 1s initial and 1 minute maximum and changes only CrashLoopBackOff, not image pull backoff
critical.heading: Alpha

critical.constraint: When a per-node max is set, it takes precedence over the reduced KEP-4603 defaults
critical.heading: Conflict resolution

tasks.task: Write Job controller unit tests for the FailIndex pod failure policy action from KEP-3850. Cover an Indexed Job with backoffLimitPerIndex whose podFailurePolicy mixes FailIndex with the existing Ignore, FailJob and Count actions, and assert .status.failedIndexes, the per-index failure count on replacement pods and the final Job condition.

required.heading: Job API
required.why: FailIndex constant, backoffLimitPerIndex and maxFailedIndexes rules, failedIndexes format, backoffLimit default

required.heading: Tracking the number of failures per index
required.why: failure count annotation, when an index fails, Ignore does not increment

required.heading: Job completion
required.why: when the Job gets Complete or Failed

required.heading: FailIndex action
required.why: FailIndex adds the index to .status.failedIndexes, only with backoffLimitPerIndex

required.heading: JobSpec API
required.why: semantics of Ignore, FailJob, Count and of onExitCodes / onPodConditions matching

required.heading: Evaluation
required.why: rules evaluated in order, first match wins, terminating pods skipped

critical.constraint: backoffLimitPerIndex requires completionMode=Indexed and restartPolicy=Never; when it is set, backoffLimit defaults to max int32
critical.heading: Job API

critical.constraint: .status.failedIndexes uses the compressed range format, for example 1,3-5,7
critical.heading: Job API

critical.constraint: The count lives in the pod annotation batch.kubernetes.io/job-index-failure-count; the index fails when it reaches backoffLimitPerIndex
critical.heading: Tracking the number of failures per index

critical.constraint: A failure that matches an Ignore rule does not increment the annotation on the replacement pod
critical.heading: Tracking the number of failures per index

critical.constraint: The Job is Complete only if all indexes succeed; it gets Failed if any index failed, once all indexes finish or maxFailedIndexes is exceeded
critical.heading: Job completion

critical.constraint: FailIndex can only be used when backoffLimitPerIndex is set
critical.heading: FailIndex action

critical.constraint: onExitCodes skips containers that exited 0, and value 0 is not allowed with the In operator
critical.heading: JobSpec API

critical.constraint: Rules are evaluated in order and only the first matching rule applies; with no match the failure is counted by default
critical.heading: Evaluation

critical.constraint: Terminating pods that are not yet Failed are not evaluated against the policy and are not replaced
critical.heading: Evaluation

tasks.task: For KEP-4412, add kubelet unit tests showing that the ensure-secret-pulled-images check (KEP-2535) handles images pulled through a credential provider that uses service account tokens: a second pod with the same service account reuses the image, while a pod with a different service account, or with a deleted and recreated service account, must pull again.

required.heading: How will this work with the Ensure secret pull images KEP?
required.why: expected behavior for same, different and recreated service accounts and the tracked coordinates

required.heading: Summary
required.why: what a failed verification means for IfNotPresent and Never pull policies

required.heading: Credential Verification Policies
required.why: which images are verified under each policy

required.heading: Writing to the Cache
required.why: ImagePullManager interface and the record/check contract the tests drive

required.heading: Beta
required.why: feature gate name, on by default, default policy

critical.constraint: Image access is tracked by service account namespace, name and UID only, not by annotations or audience
critical.heading: How will this work with the Ensure secret pull images KEP?

critical.constraint: A recreated service account has a new UID, so access to the previously pulled image must be re-verified
critical.heading: How will this work with the Ensure secret pull images KEP?

critical.constraint: When verification fails, IfNotPresent re-pulls the image and Never fails container creation; Always is unchanged
critical.heading: Summary

critical.heading: Credential Verification Policies

critical.constraint: Every RecordPullIntent must be matched by exactly one RecordImagePulled or RecordImagePullFailed; MustAttemptImagePull returns true only when the policy demands verification and no record matches

critical.constraint: The kubelet gate is KubeletEnsureSecretPulledImages, beta and enabled by default
critical.heading: Beta

tasks.task: For KEP-3866, implement the startup cleanup that removes leftover nftables rules when kube-proxy runs in iptables or ipvs mode, and count cleanup failures in the metric the KEP defines for it. Add an e2e test that switches a node from iptables to nftables mode and back.

required.heading: Tables
required.why: kube-proxy owns one table per family (ip, ip6) and must leave other tables alone

required.heading: Switching between kube-proxy modes
required.why: what each mode cleans up at startup and how the nftables cleanup must be written

required.heading: Can the feature be disabled once it has been enabled (i.e. can we roll back the enablement)?
required.why: stale rules keep intercepting traffic; which versions can clean up

required.heading: Were upgrade and rollback tested? Was the upgrade->downgrade->upgrade path tested?
required.why: the switch sequence and expected end state the e2e test must check

required.heading: What are the SLIs (Service Level Indicators) an operator can use to determine the health of the service?
required.why: the only README place naming the cleanup failure metric

critical.constraint: Delete only the kube-proxy tables in the ip and ip6 families; never flush or touch other components' tables such as firewalld
critical.heading: Tables

critical.constraint: The cleanup in iptables/ipvs mode must run nft directly (nft delete table ip kube-proxy / ip6 kube-proxy), bypassing the nftables backend abstractions, so it works even if that code is broken
critical.heading: Switching between kube-proxy modes

critical.constraint: Starting in nftables mode deletes iptables and ipvs rules; starting in iptables or ipvs mode deletes nftables rules
critical.heading: Switching between kube-proxy modes

critical.constraint: Uncleaned nftables rules keep intercepting service traffic; only kube-proxy 1.29+ cleans them automatically
critical.heading: Can the feature be disabled once it has been enabled (i.e. can we roll back the enablement)?

critical.constraint: After switching back to iptables the kube-proxy table (both tables if dual-stack) must be gone; after switching to nftables a handful of leftover iptables chains is fine, but no iptables Service rules may remain
critical.heading: Were upgrade and rollback tested? Was the upgrade->downgrade->upgrade path tested?

critical.constraint: The metric is sync_proxy_rules_nftables_cleanup_failures_total, exposed by kube-proxy
critical.heading: What are the SLIs (Service Level Indicators) an operator can use to determine the health of the service?

tasks.task: For KEP-5419 GA in v1.38, add the kubelet counter for requested resizes at both pod and container level, and deprecate the container-only requested-resizes counter it replaces, following the Kubernetes metrics stability policy.

required.why: name, type, labels and counting rule of the new counter

required.why: its closing note fixes the deprecated metric, DeprecatedVersion and the dual-recording transition

critical.constraint: The new counter is kubelet_pod_requested_resizes_total with labels level (pod|container), resource (cpu|memory), requirement (requests|limits), operation (add|remove|increase|decrease)
critical.heading: New Metrics

critical.constraint: Each resource/requirement change is counted separately: one pod-level resize of CPU and memory requests and limits adds 4 with level=pod

critical.constraint: During the transition both metrics are recorded for container-level resizes; the old one is hidden and removed only in a later release
